concepts.note: Maldacena's 1997 AdS/CFT correspondence equates a gravity theory in anti-de Sitter space with a boundary conformal field theory, giving the best-defined nonperturbative quantum-gravity models.
concepts.title: Holographic duality

concepts.note: Hawking's 1974 calculation suggested information loss; 2019 replica-wormhole derivations of the Page curve support unitarity in holographic models, but the real-world resolution is open.
concepts.title: Black-hole information paradox

concepts.note: Ashtekar's 1986 variables and Rovelli–Smolin spin networks quantize geometry; deriving a 4D continuum limit and low-energy gravity remains open.
concepts.title: Loop quantum gravity

concepts.note: Gamma-ray-burst and gravitational-wave data constrain Lorentz violation and extra dimensions, but no Planck-scale signal has been confirmed.
concepts.title: Planck-scale phenomenology

subtopics.note: Known: general relativity and quantum field theory conflict at the Planck scale ℓ_P = √(ħG/c³) ≈ 1.6×10⁻³⁵ m, while holography supplies consistent toy models. Unknown: a background-independent, empirically confirmed 4D theory; string theory/AdS-CFT, loop quantum gravity, asymptotic safety and causal triangulation are the main programmes, and no decisive experiment exists—LIGO's 2015 detection only opened strong-field tests.
subtopics.title: Quantum gravity

concepts.note: Xenon and argon detectors see no nuclear recoils above background, pushing WIMP–nucleon limits near 10⁻⁴⁷ cm² for tens of GeV masses.
concepts.title: WIMP direct detection

concepts.note: ADMX and HAYSTAC scan microwave cavities for axion–photon conversion; only small mass windows are excluded.
concepts.title: Axion haloscopes

concepts.note: Zwicky's 1933 cluster velocities and Rubin's 1970s flat rotation curves established missing mass, later confirmed by lensing and the Bullet Cluster.
concepts.title: Galactic rotation evidence

concepts.note: Milgrom's 1983 modified-gravity fits galaxy curves but struggles with clusters and the CMB; no alternative is accepted.
concepts.title: MOND alternatives

subtopics.note: Known: about 27% of the cosmic energy density is cold, collisionless dark matter, inferred from galaxy rotation, lensing, the CMB and structure formation (Ω_DM h² ≈ 0.12). Unknown: its identity; XENONnT, LZ and PandaX direct-detection null results (2023) and axion haloscopes have not found a particle.
subtopics.title: Dark matter identity

concepts.note: Riess/Perlmutter 1998 found distant SNe Ia dimmer than expected; Λ has w = −1.
concepts.title: Cosmic acceleration

concepts.note: Planck 2018 and SH0ES 2022 disagree on H0 at ~5σ; JWST and new distance-ladder calibrations test systematics.
concepts.title: Hubble tension

concepts.note: DESI BAO data (2024–2025) favour w0waCDM over Λ at few σ when combined with SNe, but no discovery is established.
concepts.title: DESI evolving dark energy

concepts.note: Euclid (launched 2023) and Rubin/LSST will map weak lensing and BAO to test w(z) and the tension.
concepts.title: Euclid and LSST

subtopics.note: Known: cosmic expansion accelerates, and ΛCDM fits CMB, BAO and supernovae with dark energy ~68% and w = p/(ρc²) ≈ −1; the decisive discovery was the 1998 supernova result. Unknown: whether w evolves and whether the ~5σ Hubble tension (local ~73 versus CMB ~67.4 km/s/Mpc) is new physics or systematics; DESI 2024–2025 hints at evolving dark energy only at low significance.
subtopics.title: Dark energy and Hubble tension

concepts.note: ATLAS and CMS found a ~125 GeV scalar in 2012; its couplings match the Standard Model, while the hierarchy problem remains open.
concepts.title: Higgs boson discovery

concepts.note: No supersymmetric particles or extra dimensions have appeared; gluino and squark limits reach the multi-TeV scale.
concepts.title: LHC null results

concepts.note: LHCb saw B-meson anomalies around 2014–2022, but 2022 data reduced their significance; the status is unresolved.
concepts.title: Flavor anomalies

concepts.note: Fermilab's 2021 measurement confirmed the Brookhaven muon g-2 discrepancy, but theory uncertainty prevents a BSM claim.
concepts.title: Muon g-2 anomaly

subtopics.note: Known: the Standard Model gauge group SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1) fits collider data, and the 2012 Higgs discovery completed its particle content; it still cannot explain neutrino masses, dark matter, baryon asymmetry, the hierarchy or gravity. Unknown: which extension is realized and at what scale; the LHC has found no SUSY or extra dimensions, so searches continue at HL-LHC, Belle II, LHCb, EDM and dark-sector experiments.
subtopics.title: Beyond the Standard Model

concepts.note: The PMNS formula P(νe→νμ) = sin²2θ sin²(Δm²L/4E) fits solar, atmospheric, reactor and beam data.
concepts.title: Neutrino oscillation

concepts.note: NOvA and T2K mildly favour normal ordering, but JUNO and DUNE must settle it; not yet a discovery.
concepts.title: Mass ordering

concepts.note: Neutrinoless double-beta searches (CUORE, LEGEND, KamLAND-Zen) have seen no signal, so whether the neutrino is its own antiparticle is open.
concepts.title: Majorana versus Dirac

concepts.note: KATRIN's 2022 limit is mβ < 0.8 eV, while cosmology gives Σmν ≲ 0.1 eV; the absolute scale remains unknown.
concepts.title: Absolute neutrino mass

subtopics.note: Known: neutrinos oscillate, so at least two masses are nonzero; Super-Kamiokande (1998) and SNO (2001) established atmospheric and solar oscillations, and mixing angles and Δm² are measured. Unknown: absolute mass scale, ordering, Dirac versus Majorana nature and leptonic CP violation; JUNO, DUNE, KATRIN and neutrinoless double-beta experiments target them.
subtopics.title: Neutrino masses and nature

concepts.note: Bednorz and Müller discovered cuprate superconductivity in 1986; the pseudogap and pairing mechanism remain contested.
concepts.title: High-Tc cuprates

concepts.note: Twisted bilayer graphene at the magic angle (2018) shows correlated insulators and superconductivity, a tunable flat-band laboratory.
concepts.title: Magic-angle graphene

concepts.note: Cuprates and heavy fermions show resistivity linear in T down to low temperature, violating Fermi-liquid expectations; its origin is open.
concepts.title: Strange metal

concepts.note: The 1982 Tsui–Störmer discovery revealed fractionally charged anyons and topological order; braiding remains a quantum-computing goal.
concepts.title: Fractional quantum Hall

subtopics.note: Known: strong electron correlations produce Mott insulators, high-Tc cuprates, fractional quantum Hall states and quantum spin liquids, often described by Hubbard-type models H = −tΣ c†c + UΣ n↑n↓. Unknown: the cuprate pairing mechanism, strange-metal transport and how to design room-temperature superconductors; ARPES, STM, neutron scattering, cold atoms and moiré systems are the main probes, with magic-angle graphene (2018) the latest decisive platform.
subtopics.title: Strongly correlated quantum matter

concepts.note: Sycamore's 2019 random-circuit sampling claim was contested by improved classical simulations; practical advantage is still unproven.
concepts.title: Quantum advantage

concepts.note: Below the threshold p < p_th, logical error falls exponentially with code distance; Willow demonstrated this in 2024 but with small logical qubits.
concepts.title: Surface-code threshold

concepts.note: Rydberg-atom arrays offer flexible connectivity and hundreds of qubits, but gate fidelities and fault tolerance are not yet sufficient.
concepts.title: Neutral-atom arrays

concepts.note: Feynman's 1982 proposal underlies analog and digital simulation of materials and chemistry; a clear beyond-classical useful result is still open.
concepts.title: Quantum simulation

subtopics.note: Known: qubits support high-fidelity gates, and small surface-code logical qubits now suppress errors as distance grows, with Google's 2024 Willow result operating below threshold after the 2019 Sycamore quantum-advantage claim. Unknown: a large fault-tolerant machine with verified practical advantage; superconducting, trapped-ion, neutral-atom and photonic platforms are racing, and error rates, scaling and verification remain open.
subtopics.title: Quantum computing and simulation

concepts.note: Magnetic fusion needs nTτ_E above the D–T ignition threshold; inertial fusion uses areal density and ρR.
concepts.title: Lawson criterion

concepts.note: The 2022 shot produced more fusion energy than laser energy on target, but wall-plug gain and repetition rate remain far off.
concepts.title: NIF ignition

concepts.note: ITER aims at Q=10 but its revised baseline delays first plasma to 2034 and D–T to 2039.
concepts.title: Tokamaks and ITER

concepts.note: Commonwealth Fusion's SPARC, TAE and others target net energy in the 2030s; no private plant has demonstrated net electricity.
concepts.title: Private fusion

subtopics.note: Known: D–T fusion can exceed target gain, with NIF achieving ignition (3.15 MJ from 2.05 MJ) in 2022 and JET setting a 69 MJ D–T record in 2024; the Lawson criterion nTτ_E ≳ 3×10²¹ keV s m⁻³ sets the target. Unknown: sustained net electricity, tritium breeding, materials and economics; ITER (revised first plasma 2034), SPARC, Wendelstein 7-X and private tokamaks are the main programmes.
subtopics.title: Controlled fusion energy

concepts.note: Carleo and Troyer (2017) represented many-body wavefunctions with restricted Boltzmann machines, launching ML-based quantum simulation.
concepts.title: Neural quantum states

concepts.note: Deep networks tag jets and search for anomalies at the LHC, but no new particle has been found this way.
concepts.title: ML for colliders

concepts.note: Raissi et al. (2019) embedded PDE residuals in loss functions, enabling data-driven solutions of physical systems.
concepts.title: Physics-informed networks

concepts.note: Survey classifiers and generative models handle billions of galaxies and transients; interpretability and selection biases remain open.
concepts.title: AI in astronomy

subtopics.note: Known: machine learning is standard in collider event selection, gravitational-wave denoising, survey astronomy, materials screening and neural quantum states, and physics-informed networks solve PDEs; the variational principle E[ψ]=⟨ψ|H|ψ⟩/⟨ψ|ψ⟩ ≥ E0 underlies neural wavefunctions. Unknown: whether ML can discover new fundamental laws or deliver calibrated uncertainty and interpretability; no AI-discovered fundamental law exists as of 2026, with Carleo–Troyer neural quantum states (2017) a landmark physics-specific result.
subtopics.title: Machine learning in physics
